newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall 4.10 pct on foreign fund sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall 4.10 pct on foreign fund sales.

text.p: Sustained foreign sales of Thai stocks put heavy pressure on the market with the SET Index declining 4.10 percent by mid-Thursday afternoon, brokers said.
They said heavy capitalised banks and finance companies led the rapid fall with the index retreating further to 1,013.22, or 4.29 percent down, at 0812 GMT.

Brokers said the market was hit by negative rumours about Thailand's economic outlook, including rumours that Standard & Poor's Corp is in the process of reviewing, with a possible downgrade, of Thailand's long-term debt rating. There has been so statement so far from the ratings agency on this. Sentiment was also eroded by statements by IBCA, the European credit rating agency, in the past week that Thailand's four top banks may be affected by a deterioration in the Thai economy, they added.
"Foreigners are selling as they don't have enough confidence in the Thai economy and on Thai politics," said Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia.
Samart said foreigners were concerned that any new government to be formed after general elections on November 17 may not enjoy stability.
